headline: Only Karpathy is worth clicking today
summary: Karpathy's HackerTube, built with Opus 5.5, is all over the HN front page; GitHub data shows agents are rewriting the pace of development.

items.title: HackerTube: Karpathy's HN video site
items.pitch: Karpathy built a site with Opus 5.5 that gathers YouTube videos recommended on HN, and yesterday it shot straight to number one on the front page.
why: 2,118 points and 515 comments on HN, so it's not just self-indulgence
The HackerBooks side project also hit 678 points, same playbook for book lists
Good reference point: here's what one person plus an agent can ship in a day now
actions: Open https://karpathy.bearblog.dev and https://hackerbooks.org and spend five minutes on each
If you want to copy it, just paste "build a comp-industry version of HackerBooks" into Claude Code
deep_dive: It's not an AI tool, it's a finished product someone built with an agent; what's useful to you is the productivity reference, not the features.
Pure web page, opens on mobile, nothing to install; downside is the content skews programmer taste, and HackerBooks fits you better than the video site.
The real takeaway: next weekend, have Claude Code build a small site along these lines and you'll find the bar is lower than you think.
items.signals: HN 2,118 points / 515 comments · HackerBooks 678 points / 157 comments · swyx says Karpathy used Opus 5.5 at medium

items.title: GitHub: agents tripled merged PRs
items.pitch: GitHub's annual data says agent-written code pushed merged PRs to 220 million a month and commits to 7.38 billion a month, both triple within a year.
why: Merged PRs tripled since the start of the year, hitting 220M/month
New repos at 30.3M/month, doubled; commits at 7.38B/month
The signal for you: writing code is becoming a default ability
items.signals: GitHub Octoverse 2026 · merged PRs 220M/month · commits 7.38B/month · new repos 30.3M/month · live notes from Simon Willison
